```text
type Engine struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Engine is the daemon. Create it with New or FromApp.

func FromApp(a *app.App, mods ...func(*Deps)) *Engine
    FromApp wires an engine to the App's real components; mods then change its
    Deps (the daemon's wiring sets the gate's eval seams there).

func New(d Deps) *Engine
    New returns an engine over d.

func (e *Engine) Kick()
    Kick asks the running loop for a tick now (what SIGUSR1 does).

func (e *Engine) PauseTool(ctx context.Context, p pipeline.Pause)
    PauseTool is pauseTool for the pipeline (Runner.OnPause): a reviewer's run
    that proved its kind logged out or over its limit pauses the kind while the
    round goes on.

func (e *Engine) Planned() []PlannedOp
    Planned returns what a dry run would have done (empty otherwise).

func (e *Engine) ReleaseEval(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR) error
    ReleaseEval closes the agents of an eval round's PR and its workspace.
    An agent herdr shows still at work (the judge finishing its turn after it
    wrote its result: turnTail) is interrupted first, the judge with one ctrl+c,
    which ends its turn as a cut own pass does, another agent with esc, and
    awaited up to abortQuietWait. Then the PR is parked (agents.Manager.Park,
    which closes the workspace; the conversations stay resumable in the agents'
    own history). When Park refuses, an agent still working, the replay's own
    workspaces (labelled "eval <repo>#<N>", holding the PR's sessions) are
    closed with whatever still runs there: they hold nothing to keep. The error
    names every workspace that stays open.

func (e *Engine) Run(ctx context.Context, opts Options) error
    Run is the daemon: lock, pidfile, startup, then a tick every
    daemon.poll_interval (or on Kick/SIGUSR1) until ctx ends or SIGTERM.
    It returns nil when another daemon holds the lock ("already running"),
    so launchd does not restart it in a loop, but ErrOpsLockHeld when a magnum
    command holds it for in-process slot work, and ErrSchemaChanged when the
    registry was migrated under it, so launchd starts it again. A dry run takes
    neither the lock nor the pidfile (it changes nothing a real daemon could
    see).

func (e *Engine) RunEval(ctx context.Context, c EvalCase) (pipeline.RoundResult, store.PR, error)
    RunEval runs one blind dry-run round for c and returns the pipeline's
    result and the agents' PR row (for Release). It refuses an engine whose
    layout has no Scratch, so a replay never writes the live registry, reports
    or notes. It closes the workspaces earlier replays of the PR left open
    (closeEvalLeftovers), runs the engine's own round preparation (preflight,
    pane environment, workspace "eval <repo>#<N>", agents, readiness probes),
    checks that every session works in that workspace (evalSessionsIn) and runs
    the pipeline, then stops: no pause, refund, toast or dismissal follows,
    those belong to the PR's real rounds. The registry rows it seeds (repo,
    PR in claiming, a per-PR slot at Checkout) live in the scratch store.

func (e *Engine) Tick(ctx context.Context) error
    Tick runs one iteration of the daemon loop. Steps log their own
    failures; the returned error joins them for the caller's information.
    A registry migrated by another binary stops the tick before any step
    (ErrSchemaChanged), and so does an idle restart (restartForBuild): on a new
    build (ErrRestartForBuild, restart_on_new_build), a landed skill version
    (ErrRestartForLearn) or a saved config (ErrRestartForConfig).

type EvalCase struct {
	Owner, Repo string
	Number      int
	URL         string
	Head        string // the pinned head, checked out in Checkout
	BaseRef     string // the PR's base branch ("" = DefaultBranch)
	// DefaultBranch is the repository's default branch.
	DefaultBranch string
	Title, Author string
	AuthorType    string // "User" or "Bot" ("" = User)
	Checkout      string // absolute path of the worktree at Head
	MainClone     string // the clone the worktree belongs to
	Watch         config.Watch
	Identity      string // the posting identity whose rights the judge checks (it posts nothing)
	// Worktrees is the directory that holds every replay's worktree,
	// Checkout among them (magnum eval: state/eval/wt). A workspace
	// labelled as a replay of this PR whose panes all work under it is one
	// an earlier replay left open, closed before this one starts ("" =
	// Checkout alone).
	Worktrees string
	// Notes gives every role the scratch copy of the repository notes
	// (paths.Layout.Notes under Scratch; the caller copies the live file).
	Notes bool
	// JudgeOnly runs the judge alone on Reports, the reviewer reports of an
	// earlier full replay of the case, which the caller copied into the
	// round's report directory (paths.Layout.ReviewDir of the scratch
	// layout, each under its role's ReportFile): the reviewers' runs are
	// seeded as round evalReportsRound's, verified with those files (a
	// Missing one as a run that did not verify), and the judge reviews as
	// in the full replay, its own pass included as configured.
	JudgeOnly bool
	Reports   []agents.Report
}
    EvalCase is one replay of `magnum eval run`: a PR at a pinned head that the
    caller already checked out (detached) in Checkout, reviewed by the watch's
    roles as a blind dry run. The PR fields come from GitHub; nothing here is
    written to the live registry.

type EvalGateOptions struct {
	Candidate string
	JudgeOnly bool
	RunDir    string
	AgentTag  string
}
    EvalGateOptions are one replay of the gate (evalrun.Options' part the gate
    sets): the directory whose prompts and judge skill it reads (the gate's
    worktree of the base for a baseline, the proposal's worktree for the
    candidate), whether the judge alone reviews (on the reviewers' reports of
    the case's newest full replay whose reviewers read what this one's would),
    and the run it belongs to, its directory under Layout.Eval and its agent tag
    (eval.AgentTag), both its own.

type EvidenceCounts struct {
	Probed         int `json:"probed"`
	Read           int `json:"read"`
	Skipped        int `json:"skipped"`
	Unknown        int `json:"unknown"`
	Stale          int `json:"stale"`
	FilesNeverRead int `json:"files_never_read"`
}
    EvidenceCounts counts a map's entries by state, and the paths no round ever
    read or probed (FilesNeverRead: only unknown or skipped entries, a stale
    entry counting as what it was).

func (c EvidenceCounts) Sentence() string
    Sentence is the card's line: "41 behaviours probed, 12 read, 9 unknown,
    4 stale (3 files never read)", the skipped ones only when there are any.

type EvidenceMap struct {
	PR string `json:"pr"` // owner/repo#N
	// HeadSHA is the head of the last round merged in, from which the next
	// one measures what changed; Round is that round.
	HeadSHA   string             `json:"head_sha"`
	Round     int                `json:"round"`
	UpdatedAt time.Time          `json:"updated_at"`
	Entries   []EvidenceMapEntry `json:"entries"`
}
    EvidenceMap is a PR's evidence map: what its rounds examined, merged.

func ReadEvidenceMap(path string) (m EvidenceMap, ok bool, err error)
    ReadEvidenceMap reads the evidence map at path (pipeline.EvidenceMapPath);
    ok is false when there is none.

func (m EvidenceMap) Counts() EvidenceCounts
    Counts counts m's entries (EvidenceCounts).

type EvidenceMapEntry struct {
	pipeline.EvidenceEntry
	Was   string `json:"was,omitempty"`
	Head  string `json:"head"`
	Round int    `json:"round"`
	Run   string `json:"run,omitempty"` // the round's judge run
}
    EvidenceMapEntry is an entry of a judge's evidence file with the head and
    the round that wrote it. A stale entry (pipeline.EvidenceStale) keeps the
    state it was written with in Was.

type FixCommit struct {
	SHA     string // 7 to 40 hex digits, as the fixer wrote it
	Message string
}
    FixCommit is a commit the fixer says it pushed.

type FixOff struct {
	Since time.Time `json:"since"`
	By    string    `json:"by"`
}
    FixOff is a PR's opt-out of the fix job: when it was set and by whom
    ("magnum fix --off").

func ParseFixOff(s string) (FixOff, bool)
    ParseFixOff reads a KVPRFixOff value; ok is false for one that is not an
    opt-out.

type FixPayload struct {
	PRTarget
	DryRun bool `json:"dry_run,omitempty"`
	Off    bool `json:"off,omitempty"`
	On     bool `json:"on,omitempty"`
}
    FixPayload is a `magnum fix` request: start a fix loop on the PR (DryRun:
    answer what would happen and do nothing), or switch the fix job off for it
    (Off: autofix leaves it alone, KVPRFixOff) or on again (On). Neither Off nor
    On starts a loop.

type FixReport struct {
	// Pushed are the commits on GitHub, none for "nothing".
	Pushed []FixCommit
	// Replied is the line that counts the threads the fixer replied in, as
	// written ("N threads (a fixed, b already fixed, c not a bug, d won't
	// fix)").
	Replied string
	// NeedsYou are the findings that need the author, one entry per line
	// without its "- " (`<comment id> <priority> <path>:<line>: <reason>`),
	// none for "none".
	NeedsYou []string
	// PushFailed: the fixer says its push failed ("push failed: …").
	PushFailed bool
	// Description are the changes to the PR description ("description:
	// <what changed>" lines under "## Pushed"), what changed per line.
	Description []string
}
    FixReport is what the fixer reports.

func ParseFixReport(text string, runID string) (FixReport, error)
    ParseFixReport reads the fixer's report of the run runID.

    The first line must be the run's marker (agents.ReportMarker),
    else the error is ErrFixReportMarker. The three sections must all follow,
    in order, each with something under its heading, else the error is
    ErrFixReportPartial; text before the first heading is ignored. The first
    two sections run to the next heading. "## Needs you" runs to the next
    heading or, after a blank line, to the first line that is not a "- " entry,
    so a loose list (a blank line between entries) keeps all of its entries and
    a closing remark after the sections is ignored. Any other line that does not
    fit its section is an error that quotes the line (not a sentinel).

type FixState struct {
	Cycle        int       `json:"cycle"`
	Cap          int       `json:"cap"`
	Phase        string    `json:"phase"`
	Since        string    `json:"since"`
	Head         string    `json:"head"`
	By           string    `json:"by"`
	Report       string    `json:"report"`
	StartedAt    time.Time `json:"started_at"`
	NeedsYou     []string  `json:"needs_you,omitempty"`
	Answered     []string  `json:"answered,omitempty"`
	Role         string    `json:"role,omitempty"`
	ForcedAt     time.Time `json:"forced_at,omitzero"`
	Held         bool      `json:"held,omitempty"`
	Context      string    `json:"context,omitempty"`
	OthersUnread string    `json:"others_unread,omitempty"`
}
    FixState is where a PR's fix loop is: cycle Cycle of at most Cap, in Phase.
    Since is the head the loop started from and Head the head the current
    cycle fixes (in phase reviewing, the head the fixer pushed). By says who
    started it ("magnum fix", "autofix"), Role is the fix role whose fixer
    runs the current cycle, Report is the path of the report the fixer writes,
    and StartedAt is when the loop started. NeedsYou are the findings a fixer
    that pushed left to the author (its report's "## Needs you" entries,
    in its own words, so never put in an event or a log; FixCalls reads what
    each asks): the push is re-reviewed first, and the loop ends after that
    round as needs attention, unless magnum's threads show every call settled
    by then (freshNeedsYou), when the round decides the loop as for a push that
    left nothing to the author. Answered are the comment ids of the threads
    of magnum's among them that showed their answer at the settle, whose
    calls ask only for the resolution; fixReReview writes it with NeedsYou,
    and an id whose entry is gone asks nothing. ForcedAt is when the loop forced
    the re-review of its push (phase reviewing): its re-review is the forced
    round dispatched at or after it, and every other round that ends while the
    loop waits is ignored (fixAfterRound; zero in a row written before it was
    recorded, where any forced round is). Held says that re-review ended and
    called for a next cycle a drain for a restart refused: no round that ends
    afterwards is the loop's re-review, and the restart's recovery, or the
    drain's end without one, starts that cycle (recoverReviewingLoop). Context
    is what the current cycle did to the fixer's conversation it resumed before
    its prompt, in a few words (fixCompact: "compacted 82% → 31%", "compacted
    from 82%" when the pane shows no figure after it, "fresh session (82% after
    /compact)", "fresh session (/compact failed)"); "" when it resumed it as
    it was or started a fresh fixer anyway. OthersUnread says that the current
    cycle's fixer did not get all the other reviewers' items (writeExternal):
    "not read (HTTP 502)", "not all read (over 1000 review threads)", a short
    cause and never PR text; the loop's end says so (othersUnread). "" when it
    got them.

func ParseFixState(s string) (FixState, bool)
    ParseFixState reads a KVPRFix value; ok is false for one that is not a fix
    loop.

func (s FixState) Short() string
    Short is the loop while its fixer works, as the board's state cell shows it:
    "fixing 1/3 · claude-fix" ("fixing 1/3" when the role is not known).

type GateCase struct {
	learn.GateRow
	BaselineRun  string `json:"baseline_run,omitempty"`
	CandidateRun string `json:"candidate_run,omitempty"` // a second replay's when Retried
	SecondRun    string `json:"second_run,omitempty"`    // a won miss target's second replay (learn.GateRow.Confirm)
	ReportsRun   string `json:"reports_run,omitempty"`
}
    GateCase is one case of a gate's result: the row learn.Judge read,
    the eval runs its two scores come from (a guard's stored baseline's run, or
    the base's once the candidate lost it twice), the run of a won miss target's
    second replay and, judge-only, the full replay whose reviewer reports both
    judges read.

type GateMark struct {
	Proposal int64     `json:"proposal"`
	Started  time.Time `json:"started"`
}
    GateMark is the gate in flight (KVLearnGating).

type GateResult struct {
	State          string     `json:"state"`
	Rule           string     `json:"rule"`
	Mode           string     `json:"mode"`
	Inputs         string     `json:"inputs,omitempty"`
	BaselineInputs string     `json:"baseline_inputs,omitempty"`
	Cases          []GateCase `json:"cases"`
	Runs           []string   `json:"runs,omitempty"`
	CorpusError    string     `json:"corpus_error,omitempty"`
}
    GateResult is what a proposal's gate decided (learn_proposals.gate_json):
    the verdict and its rule, the mode, the inputs hashes the candidate and the
    baseline replayed with (eval.Run.Inputs), every case, the eval runs the gate
    stored and why the corpus could not be read, if it could not.

type Git interface {
	MergeBase(ctx context.Context, dir, a, b string) (string, error)
	FindClone(ctx context.Context, cloneRoot, owner, name string) (string, error)
	// RevParse and FetchCommit find the first parent of a merged PR's merge
	// commit, the base a post-merge round reviews from (postMergeBase).
	RevParse(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) (string, error)
	FetchCommit(ctx context.Context, mainClone, sha string, number int) error
	// ChangedUnder tells whether a head changes the project config a
	// running agent reloads (parkReloading).
	ChangedUnder(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head string, paths ...string) ([]string, error)
	// DiffStat measures the PR's size at a full pass's baseline, in the
	// round's checkout (prSize, fullpass.go).
	DiffStat(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head string) ([]gitx.FileStat, error)
	// ChangedBetween names the files that differ between two heads: the
	// PR's evidence map marks what they held stale (evidence.go).
	ChangedBetween(ctx context.Context, dir, from, to string) ([]string, error)
	// FetchBranch and MergeConflicts tell the fix job whether the head its
	// fixer starts from conflicts with the PR's base (baseConflict): the
	// base branch fetched into the slot's main clone, then `git merge-tree`
	// of the head and that tip.
	FetchBranch(ctx context.Context, mainClone, base string) error
	MergeConflicts(ctx context.Context, dir, head, base string) ([]string, error)
	// IsAncestor tells the fix job's settle whether the head the fixer
	// pushed descends from the PR row's head, a push the poller saw during
	// the run (the base merge `magnum fix-sync` replayed onto: recordFixPush).
	IsAncestor(ctx context.Context, dir, ancestor, rev string) (bool, error)
}
    Git is the part of *gitx.Client the engine reads (round context, clone
    discovery for repos.clone_path).

type GitHub interface {
	Radar(ctx context.Context, org string) ([]github.RepoRadar, github.RateLimit, error)
	// CIStates reads the head rollups (state and counts by state) of the
	// watched repositories' open PRs on every poll (readCI, poll.go); the
	// radar carries none.
	CIStates(ctx context.Context, prs []github.PRRadar) (map[string]github.CIState, github.RateLimit, error)
	Details(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, numbers []int) (map[int]github.PRDetails, []int, error)
	// ReviewAnswers reads what the inline comments of reviews answer, by
	// node id: the reviews since magnum's latest review that Details left
	// unresolved (resolveAnswers, poll.go).
	ReviewAnswers(ctx context.Context, ids []string) (map[string]github.ReviewAnswer, error)
	ConfirmStates(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, numbers []int) (map[int]github.PRState, []int, error)
	Compare(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, base, head string) (github.CompareStats, error)
	// CompareFiles reads base...head's changed files with their patches
	// (the PR's own diff against its base, base_merge.go; triage; reruns).
	CompareFiles(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, base, head string) ([]github.FileDelta, error)
	// ComparePush is CompareFiles with GitHub's status and whether the
	// range has a merge commit (the trivial-delta check, delta.go).
	ComparePush(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, base, head string) (github.PushComparison, error)
	// ReviewsWithMarker with an empty marker lists a PR's last 30 reviews:
	// the since_review fallback when Details' latestReviews was truncated.
	ReviewsWithMarker(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, marker string) ([]github.Review, error)
	// AllReviews lists every review of a PR and whether the list is
	// complete: what a former identity left standing (dismissFormer).
	AllReviews(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) ([]github.Review, bool, error)
	DismissReview(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, reviewID int64, message string) error
	// CreateReview posts a manual verdict (verdict.go).
	CreateReview(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, commitID, event, body string) (github.RESTReview, error)
	// RequiredChecks reads the checks a branch requires (required.go).
	RequiredChecks(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, branch string) ([]string, bool, error)
	// CommitChecks reads a commit's checks: auto-approval's read of a
	// PR's base tip, whose failing checks do not hold the approval of a
	// head that fails them too (autoapprove_ci_base.go).
	CommitChecks(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, sha string) ([]github.Check, error)
	// CreateIssueComment and EditIssueComment post and edit a PR's review
	// status comment as its posting identity (status_comment.go).
	CreateIssueComment(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, body string) (github.IssueComment, error)
	EditIssueComment(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, commentID int64, body string) (github.IssueComment, error)
}
    GitHub is the part of *github.Client the engine uses (one client per
    identity): the poller's reads, and the dismissal of an App approval the head
    left behind (followApproval), made as the App identity.

type GitHubCost struct {
	Identity string `json:"identity"`
	// Rate is the identity's GraphQL rate limit as the daemon's calls
	// answered it: the lowest live reading (observe), or 0 left after a
	// call GitHub refused for its rate limit (refused); nil before the
	// first.
	Rate *GitHubRate `json:"rate,omitempty"`
	// Hours are the clock hours with calls among the last 24, oldest first.
	Hours []GitHubHour `json:"hours"`
	// Windows are the GraphQL rate-limit windows the daemon's calls answered
	// in, oldest reset first, until 24 hours after their reset.
	Windows []GitHubWindow `json:"windows,omitempty"`
}
    GitHubCost is the meter's record of one identity (KVGitHubCost).

func ParseGitHubCost(s string) (GitHubCost, bool)
    ParseGitHubCost reads a KVGitHubCost value (ok false for one that does not
    read).

func (c GitHubCost) Since(from time.Time) (GitHubOpCost, []GitHubOpSum)
    Since sums the hours that started at or after from: the total points,
    calls and REST calls, and the ops by points, the costliest first (by calls,
    then by name, among equal points).

type GitHubHour struct {
	Hour      time.Time `json:"hour"`       // the hour's start, UTC
	Points    int       `json:"points"`     // GraphQL points
	Calls     int       `json:"calls"`      // every call, GraphQL and REST
	RESTCalls int       `json:"rest_calls"` // REST calls, against the core budget
	// Ops splits the hour by op (an engine label, GitHubOpWords, or a call's
	// own kind).
	Ops map[string]GitHubOpCost `json:"ops"`
}
    GitHubHour is one clock hour of an identity's calls.

type GitHubLow struct {
	Since     time.Time `json:"since"`
	Remaining int       `json:"remaining"`
	Limit     int       `json:"limit,omitempty"`
	Floor     int       `json:"floor"`
	Until     time.Time `json:"until"`
}
    GitHubLow is a run of low budget (KVGitHubLow): since when, the budget when
    it began or its reset last moved (what was left, of what limit) and the
    floor then, and when the budget resets. The start reads its budget back into
    the meter (loadGitHubCost), so a daemon that stopped before the minute's
    flush still holds the work the run held.

func ParseGitHubLow(s string) (GitHubLow, bool)
    ParseGitHubLow reads a KVGitHubLow value (ok false for one that does not
    read).

type GitHubOpCost struct {
	Points    int `json:"points"`
	Calls     int `json:"calls"`
	RESTCalls int `json:"rest_calls,omitempty"`
}
    GitHubOpCost is what one op cost in an hour.

type GitHubOpSum struct {
	Op string `json:"op"`
	GitHubOpCost
}
    GitHubOpSum is one op's cost over several hours.

type GitHubRate struct {
	Remaining int       `json:"remaining"`
	Limit     int       `json:"limit"`
	ResetAt   time.Time `json:"reset_at"`
	SeenAt    time.Time `json:"seen_at"` // when the call that answered it returned
}
    GitHubRate is a GraphQL rate limit as a call answered it.

type GitHubWindow struct {
	ResetAt time.Time `json:"reset_at"` // UTC
	Limit   int       `json:"limit"`
	// Used is the highest count of points used in the window any reading of
	// the daemon's calls gave (GitHub's used, else limit − remaining): what
	// every caller on the login or installation spent, the daemon included.
	Used int `json:"used"`
	// Points sums what the daemon's calls answered in the window cost.
	Points int `json:"points"`
	// Told: the daemon said that the window's spend outside its calls
	// reached a fifth of the limit (noteGitHubOutside).
	Told bool `json:"told,omitempty"`
}
    GitHubWindow is one GraphQL rate-limit window of an identity as the daemon's
    calls answered in it, keyed by the reset GitHub gave it first (a reading
    within 10 seconds of it is the same window): one login can show two windows
    at once (on 2026-10-21 at 19:11Z thirteen reads within 15 seconds answered
    19:29:51Z and 19:32:12Z), and calls in flight return in any order, so the
    window holds what the order cannot change.

func (w GitHubWindow) Outside() int
    Outside is what the window's readings say was spent outside the daemon's
    calls: Used − Points, never below 0. It counts what others spent before the
    daemon's first call of the window too.

type Herdr interface {
	Snapshot(ctx context.Context) (herdr.Snapshot, error)
}
    Herdr is the part of *herdr.Client the tick reads: one snapshot per tick
    (agent statuses for completion, the working-Codex gate, liveness).

type IdentityVerdictPayload struct {
	Name   string `json:"name"`
	Pass   bool   `json:"pass"`
	Reason string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
}
    IdentityVerdictPayload is the verdict of `magnum identities check` for the
    configured identity Name; Reason says why a failed check failed.

type Inventory interface {
	Scan(ctx context.Context, opts inventory.Options) (inventory.Inventory, error)
	UpsertSlotDatabases(ctx context.Context, inv inventory.Inventory) (inventory.SyncResult, error)
}
    Inventory is the reconcile scanner (*inventory.Scanner).

type KindVersion struct {
	// Version is the first line the version command printed.
	Version string `json:"version"`
	// Path is the binary read, its links resolved: the file mise's shim
	// runs (`mise which <kind>`) for a command that is one; MTime is its
	// modification time then. The version command runs again only once
	// either differs.
	Path  string    `json:"path"`
	MTime time.Time `json:"mtime"`
	// SeenAt is when the version was read.
	SeenAt time.Time `json:"seen_at"`
	// Previous and ChangedAt are the version before the last change and
	// when the daemon read the new one (EventKindVersionChanged); empty
	// until a version changed.
	Previous  string    `json:"previous,omitempty"`
	ChangedAt time.Time `json:"changed_at,omitzero"`
}
    KindVersion is what the daemon read of an agent kind's CLI version, at its
    start and at the health checks of every tick, through the kind's command on
    its PATH as `magnum doctor` reads it (`<kind> --version`).

func (v KindVersion) ChangedWithin(now time.Time, d time.Duration) bool
    ChangedWithin reports whether the version changed within d before now.

type LandDay struct {
	Day    string `json:"day"`
	Landed int    `json:"landed"`
}
    LandDay is how many proposals landed on Day (store.DayKey).

type LearnDecisionPayload struct {
	ID     int64  `json:"id"`
	Reason string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
}
    LearnDecisionPayload is the operator's answer to a held skill proposal
    (`magnum learn --review`): land it (ReqLearnLand) or reject it
    (ReqLearnReject, a gating one's only answer) with Reason, which the next
    edit reads.

type LearnGit interface {
	RevParse(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) (string, error)
	WorktreeAdd(ctx context.Context, mainClone, path, ref string, detach bool, branch string) error
	WorktreeDiscard(ctx context.Context, repo, root, dir string) error
	StatusPaths(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]gitx.StatusEntry, error)
	CurrentBranch(ctx context.Context, repo string) (string, error)
	CommitAll(ctx context.Context, dir, message string, paths ...string) (string, error)
	ChangedPaths(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head string, pathspecs ...string) ([]string, error)
	BranchDelete(ctx context.Context, mainClone, branch string, force bool) error
	InProgress(ctx context.Context, repo string) (string, error)
	MergeBase(ctx context.Context, dir, a, b string) (string, error)
	RebaseOnto(ctx context.Context, dir, onto, upstream string) error
	ReplayConflicts(ctx context.Context, dir, onto, rev string) ([]string, error)
	PatchID(ctx context.Context, dir, rev string) (string, error)
	DirtyPaths(ctx context.Context, dir string, paths ...string) ([]string, error)
	MergeFFOnly(ctx context.Context, repo, base, branch string) error
	RestoreFrom(ctx context.Context, dir, rev string, paths ...string) error
	BranchesUnder(ctx context.Context, repo, prefix string) ([]string, error)
}
    LearnGit is the git work of an editor run, its gate and its landing
    (learn_land.go) (*gitx.Client).

type LearnProposePayload struct{}
    LearnProposePayload is a `magnum learn --propose` request.

type LearnRestartMark struct {
	Version  int64     `json:"version"`
	Proposal int64     `json:"proposal"`
	Landed   time.Time `json:"landed"`
	Manual   bool      `json:"manual,omitempty"`
}
    LearnRestartMark is the landed version the daemon waits to restart on
    (KVLearnRestart): Manual when the operator restarts it (learn restart
    manual, or no launchd to start it again).

type LearnRevertPayload struct {
	Version int64  `json:"version"`
	Reason  string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
}
    LearnRevertPayload is a `magnum learn --revert <version>` request:
    a proposal that restores the files of the version before Version, for Reason
    (the design log's entry says it).

type MachineGroup struct {
	Repo string // owner/name
	// Cmd is the command, its test-file arguments left out (machineCommand);
	// "" when the judge named none.
	Cmd string
	// Error is what the newest round said of it (untrusted agent text).
	Error string
	// Rounds counts the events (one per round) that list the command.
	Rounds int
	// First and Last are the oldest and the newest of those events.
	First, Last time.Time
}
    MachineGroup is one command failing on the review machine in the rounds of
    one repository.

func MachineGroups(evs []store.Event) []MachineGroup
    MachineGroups groups the round.environment events of evs (other kinds
    and events without a PR subject are skipped) by repository and command.
    An event counts once per group however often it lists the command; an event
    whose failures cannot be read counts as one failure without a command,
    its message the error. Most rounds come first, then the newest.

type MemorySample struct {
	// Level is kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level (MemoryNormal,
	// MemoryWarn, MemoryCritical), MemoryUnknown when it could not be read;
	// Pressure names it ("normal", "warn", "critical", "unknown").
	Level    int    `json:"level"`
	Pressure string `json:"pressure"`
	// Swap is vm.swapusage; nil when it could not be read.
	Swap      *MemorySwap `json:"swap,omitempty"`
	SampledAt time.Time   `json:"sampled_at"`
	// Cause says why the level, the swap or both are unknown ("" when both
	// were read).
	Cause string `json:"cause,omitempty"`
}
    MemorySample is one reading of the machine's memory.

func ReadMemory(ctx context.Context, r execx.Runner, now time.Time) MemorySample
    ReadMemory takes a memory sample at now through r: the pressure level and
    the swap, each read and parsed on its own, so one that fails leaves the
    other's reading in the sample (`magnum doctor` reads it so).

func (s MemorySample) SwapText() string
    SwapText is the swap as the status line, the doctor, the events and the
    toast say it: "swap 49.1 of 50.0 GB used" (GB of 2³⁰ bytes, as the disk line
    and Activity Monitor count them), or "swap unknown".

type MemorySwap struct {
	UsedBytes  int64 `json:"used_bytes"`
	TotalBytes int64 `json:"total_bytes"`
}
    MemorySwap is the swap in use and the swap files' size, in bytes.

type NotPreservedError struct {
	ID       int64
	Problems []string
}
    NotPreservedError refuses an apply that would lose lines of the notes
    (notes.CheckPreserved): such a proposal can only be rejected or curated
    again.

func (e *NotPreservedError) Error() string

type NotesApply struct {
	Live   string // the notes' fingerprint when the decider read them
	Target string // the fingerprint of the state it approved to write
	By     string // store.DecidedBy*
	// Reason is the decider's one-line reason, kept with the proposal (the
	// critic's; "" = none).
	Reason string
	Now    time.Time
	// Wait bounds the wait for the notes lock (0 = NotesLockWait).
	Wait time.Duration
}
    NotesApply is what a decider approved: the fingerprints of the notes it saw
    and of the state to write, and who it is.

type NotesCuratePayload struct {
	Repo      string `json:"repo"` // owner/name
	Supersede int64  `json:"supersede,omitempty"`
	Why       string `json:"why,omitempty"`
}
    NotesCuratePayload is a `magnum notes <repo> --curate` request, or the new
    curation `magnum notes <repo> --review` asks for instead of a stale proposal
    or one that would lose lines of the notes: Supersede is that proposal's id,
    and Why the reason it is superseded with ("" = it is stale).

type NotesHarnessChange struct {
	Name   string `json:"name"`
	Change string `json:"change"` // added | removed | changed | kept
	Action string `json:"action,omitempty"`
	Into   string `json:"into,omitempty"`
	Reason string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
}
    NotesHarnessChange is one harness file of a proposal: how it differs from
    the base, and what the curator said of it.

type NotesMergeView struct {
	Clean          bool     `json:"clean"`
	NotesConflicts []string `json:"notes_conflicts,omitempty"`   // the base version's lines both changed differently
	Conflicts      []string `json:"harness_conflicts,omitempty"` // harness files both changed in ways that do not merge
	Kept           []string `json:"harness_kept,omitempty"`      // files the proposal deletes that a round changed since: kept
	Merged         []string `json:"harness_merged,omitempty"`    // files both changed whose texts merged
}
    NotesMergeView is a stale proposal's merge with the notes' changes since.

type NotesReviewMiss struct {
	ID       int64  `json:"id"`
	Severity string `json:"severity,omitempty"`
	Where    string `json:"where,omitempty"`
	Title    string `json:"title,omitempty"`
	Outcome  string `json:"outcome"` // store.MissNoted | store.MissSkipped
	Section  string `json:"section,omitempty"`
	Reason   string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
	State    string `json:"state"` // the miss's state now
}
    NotesReviewMiss is a miss a proposal was given, and what it did with it.

type NotesReviewView struct {
	Repo     string              `json:"repo"`
	Proposal store.NotesProposal `json:"proposal"`
	Diff     string              `json:"notes_diff"`
	// ArchiveDiff is the archive's (notes.ArchiveName) unified diff, ""
	// when the proposal leaves it as it is; Harness leaves it out.
	ArchiveDiff string               `json:"archive_diff,omitempty"`
	Harness     []NotesHarnessChange `json:"harness"`
	Sections    []notes.Change       `json:"sections"`
	Misses      []NotesReviewMiss    `json:"misses"`
	Before      notes.Size           `json:"size_before"`
	After       notes.Size           `json:"size_after"`
	Expired     bool                 `json:"expired,omitempty"` // older than ProposalTTL: it can no longer be applied
	// Stale: the notes changed since the proposal was made; Merge is its
	// three-way merge with their changes, and when it is clean the diff,
	// the harness changes and the sizes are those of the merge applied to
	// the notes now.
	Stale bool            `json:"stale"`
	Merge *NotesMergeView `json:"merge,omitempty"`
	// NotPreserved is what applying the proposal would lose of the notes
	// now (PreservationProblems): a proposal with any can only be rejected
	// or curated again.
	NotPreserved []string `json:"not_preserved,omitempty"`

	// Check holds the states the review read (base, proposed, the notes now
	// and the merge); Changes the curator's changes.json.
	Check   StaleCheck    `json:"-"`
	Changes notes.Changes `json:"-"`
}
    NotesReviewView is a proposal as a review shows it.

func ReviewFrom(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, maxLine int, full string, p store.NotesProposal, check StaleCheck) (NotesReviewView, error)
    ReviewFrom is ReviewProposal from p's states as check read them (a restore
    not proposed yet has no states in the registry to read): the notes' and
    the archive's diffs, the harness changes with the curator's reasons,
    the sections, the misses it was given with what it did with them, the sizes
    before and after (of the proposal against its base, or of a clean merge
    against the notes now) and what an apply would lose.

func ReviewProposal(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, maxLine int, full string, nr notes.Repo, p store.NotesProposal) (NotesReviewView, error)
    ReviewProposal reviews proposal p of full's notes nr: its base and proposed
    states, the notes now and, when they are no longer its base (stale), its
    merge with their changes since. maxLine is notes max_line, for the sizes.

func (v NotesReviewView) Target() (notes.State, bool)
    Target is what an apply of the reviewed proposal writes: the proposed state,
    or a stale one's clean merge (false when it conflicts).

type OpenHold struct {
	Until time.Time `json:"until"`
	At    time.Time `json:"at"`
}
    OpenHold is a PR's hold by `magnum open`: At is when it was set (the open,
    or the start that converted the open's lasting pin) and Until At plus
    open_hold. Input in the PR's panes extends it (End).

func OpenHoldOf(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, prID int64) (OpenHold, bool)
    OpenHoldOf is PR prID's hold record, whether its PR is still pinned or not
    (OpenHolds).

func ParseOpenHold(s string) (OpenHold, bool)
    ParseOpenHold reads a KVPROpenHold value; ok is false for "" or a value it
    cannot read.

func (h OpenHold) End(d config.Daemon, humanAt *time.Time) time.Time
    End is when the hold ends: Until, or human_cooldown after humanAt (the PR's
    human_active_at, the last input in its panes) when that is later.

type OpenPayload struct {
	PRTarget
	Role string `json:"role,omitempty"` // a role of the PR's watch, by name or alias; "" = its judge
}
    OpenPayload is a `magnum open` request for a PR without a live session:
    the daemon gives it a slot (its own, a free pool slot or a per-PR worktree),
    checks out reviewed_sha (else the head) when the slot holds something else,
    starts or resumes the judge and Role's agent (an on-demand role gets its
    pane), pins the PR and its slot, and completes with the pane id of Role.
    A PR whose session is live, or whose round is running, completes at once.

type Options struct {
	// Once runs startup and a single tick, then keeps observing herdr only
	// until the rounds that tick launched are finished and the heavy jobs
	// queued meanwhile are done (the heavy worker runs alongside, as in the
	// daemon, so rounds are observed while heavy work runs), and returns.
	Once bool
	// NoSignals skips installing SIGTERM/SIGINT (stop) and SIGUSR1 (tick now)
	// handlers.
	NoSignals bool
	// Build is this daemon's build (CurrentBuild), recorded at startup as
	// KVDaemonBuild.
	Build Build
	// CheckBuild checks a binary found on disk before the daemon restarts on
	// it ([daemon] restart_on_new_build): it returns the binary's version, or
	// why the binary refuses the configuration. nil = no restart for a new
	// build.
	CheckBuild func(ctx context.Context, path string) (version string, err error)
	// Supervised: launchd runs this daemon and starts it again when it exits
	// non-zero, so it may exit for a new build.
	Supervised bool
	// ShellPATH is what the daemon command took from the login shell's PATH
	// before the engine was built ([daemon] shell_path), recorded at startup
	// (KVDaemonShellPATH, event daemon.shell_path); nil with the key off.
	ShellPATH *ShellPATH
}
    Options tune Run.

type PRTarget struct {
	Ref    string `json:"ref,omitempty"`
	Repo   string `json:"repo,omitempty"`
	Number int    `json:"number,omitempty"`
}
    PRTarget names a PR in a request: Repo ("owner/name") and Number win;
    otherwise Ref is any form github.ParseRef accepts, resolved against
    daemon.default_repo.

type PausePayload struct {
	Reason string     `json:"reason,omitempty"`
	Until  *time.Time `json:"until,omitempty"`
	Tool   string     `json:"tool,omitempty"`
	Watch  string     `json:"watch,omitempty"`
}
    PausePayload pauses (pause) or resumes (resume) automation. For resume,
    Tool (an agent kind such as "codex", "claude", "droid", or "all") lifts that
    kind's pause and Watch a watch owner's identity-leak pause instead of the
    daemon pause.

type PlannedOp struct {
	At      time.Time `json:"at"`
	Subject string    `json:"subject"`
	Action  string    `json:"action"`
	Detail  string    `json:"detail,omitempty"`
}
    PlannedOp is one side effect a dry run decided on but did not perform.

type ProposalDecidedError struct{ Proposal store.NotesProposal }
    ProposalDecidedError refuses an apply of a proposal that no longer waits:
    another decider applied or rejected it, or claimed it first.

func (e *ProposalDecidedError) Error() string

type ProvisionPayload struct {
	Pool  string `json:"pool,omitempty"`
	Count int    `json:"count,omitempty"`
}
    ProvisionPayload provisions Count pool slots (resuming interrupted ones
    first; Count <= 0 = up to pool.min) of the pool of repository Pool ("" =
    daemon.default_repo, else the only pool).

type Recorder struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Recorder collects a dry run's planned side effects: it logs "would …",
    keeps the ops for Engine.Planned and writes a dryrun.<action> event (into
    the dry run's private store copy).

func (r *Recorder) Ops() []PlannedOp
    Ops returns a copy of the recorded ops.

func (r *Recorder) Record(ctx context.Context, subject, action, detail string)
    Record notes one planned side effect.

type RepairPayload struct {
	Slot string `json:"slot"`
}
    RepairPayload re-runs provisioning of a free, broken, provisioning or lost
    pool slot.

type ReplyRound struct {
	Head    string    `json:"head"`
	At      time.Time `json:"at"`
	Replies int       `json:"replies"`
}
    ReplyRound is a reply round as KVPRReplyRound records it.

type ReviewPayload struct {
	PRTarget
	// Again is ignored: a forced round reviews the head even when it was
	// reviewed already. No CLI sends it any more; it stays so a request an
	// older CLI queued with --again still decodes (decode refuses unknown fields).
	Again bool `json:"again,omitempty"`
	Fresh bool `json:"fresh,omitempty"` // park the sessions and start new conversations
	// Full asks for a full pass (`magnum review --full`, fullpass.go): fresh
	// sessions, and every role reviews the whole PR again as a first review
	// does, the judge deciding every earlier thread; on a PR never reviewed
	// it is a first review as any.
	Full bool `json:"full,omitempty"`
	// Simplify asks for the role answering to "simplify" (claude-simplify
	// by default) this round, whatever its runs; kept for older CLIs, the
	// same as Roles ["simplify"].
	Simplify bool `json:"simplify,omitempty"`
	// Roles asks for these roles of the PR's watch (names or aliases) this
	// round, whatever their runs ("first" or "manual"; a "never" role is
	// refused). The daemon stores the resolved names until a review posts.
	Roles []string `json:"roles,omitempty"`
	As    string   `json:"as,omitempty"` // post as this identity from now on
	// DryRun runs the round with pipeline.RoundInput.DryRun: the judge
	// writes its planned review and posts nothing; afterwards the PR returns
	// to the state it had (reviewed_sha does not move).
	DryRun bool `json:"dry_run,omitempty"`
	// Replies asks the judge alone to re-decide the replies on its review

	// reply round, which answers in the threads unless the verdict changes.
	// It takes a head magnum reviewed and replies it has not re-decided;
	// otherwise the round is an ordinary forced one.
	Replies bool `json:"replies,omitempty"`
}

type Slots interface {
	Claim(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, pool config.Pool) (store.Slot, error)
	Checkout(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pr store.PR, pool config.Pool, targetSHA string) error
	// Fetch and CheckoutFetched split Checkout around its fetch, for a
	// round that reads the head before the checkout moves (parkReloading).
	Fetch(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pr store.PR, pool config.Pool) (string, error)
	CheckoutFetched(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pr store.PR, pool config.Pool, targetSHA, fetched string) error
	CreatePRWorktree(ctx context.Context, watch config.Watch, repo string, pr store.PR, targetSHA string) (store.Slot, error)
	Release(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool, reason string) error

	Unpin(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
	// ClearPin and Guard serve a review request of a pinned PR
	// (review_unpin.go): the pin goes, the guard's holds stay and are named.
	ClearPin(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
	Guard(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
	// Resync puts the slot back in order after the fix job's fixer committed
	// in it: detached at sha (the pushed head, or the old one), recorded as
	// checked out.
	Resync(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, sha string) error
	// Reserve, Repair and Adopt serve the open, repair and adopt requests.
	Reserve(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, pool config.Pool) (store.Slot, error)
	Repair(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool) error
	Adopt(ctx context.Context, pool config.Pool, path string) (store.Slot, error)
	// CheckSchema, ForgetSchema and RecordSchema decide and record a round's
	// schema reload (readinessPlan), ResetFailed counts a reload that failed
	// (RecordSchema clears the count); EnsureSchema reloads for magnum open.
	CheckSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool) (slots.SchemaCheck, error)
	ForgetSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
	RecordSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, c slots.SchemaCheck) error
	ResetFailed(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, cause string) (int, error)
	EnsureSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool) (string, error)
}

    ("re-review · retry 2/3 → 22:57"); any other wait is its Short.

    until 00:00; `magnum review talkable#729` runs it now". ref is how the PR is
    named on the command line.

func (w Wait) Short(now time.Time) string

    00:00", "re-review · quiet → 14:09", "review · codex paused → 15:00",
    "re-review · small delta 8/30 lines → 16:40", "re-review · requested by
    alice → now", "delta check · quiet → 14:09", "re-review · retry 2/3 setup →
    22:57", "re-review · pinned → u" (u: the screens' unpin key), "re-review ·
    held → 03:21" (an open's hold, which ends by itself).

```

## eval

```text
package eval // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/eval"

Package eval scores an evaluation replay of magnum's pull request review against
a corpus of pull requests with known ("seeded") defects.

The corpus (corpus.go) lists, per pull request, the reviewed head and the
defects a good review must report. The judge's result file of a no-post run
(findings.go) is parsed into findings, and ScoreCase (score.go) tells which
defects were found, at which severity, and how many findings matched nothing
(noise). Runs (report.go) collect the scores of one replay, persist them, can be
rescored after the corpus is corrected, and render a text or markdown report.

The package is pure: it starts no process, touches no network and knows nothing
of the registry. Its only file access is the corpus file and the run directories
it is told about.

CONSTANTS

const (
	ExpectFound  = "found"
	ExpectAbsent = "absent"
)
    What a review is expected to do with a defect (Defect.Expect): report it,
    the default, or not report it, a finding an author declined as wrong (a
    match is a false positive, Score.AbsentHits).

const (
	// OutcomeFlagged: the case is not replayed, since an earlier replay of
	// it or of its PR was refused or the live registry holds a Codex flag
	// for its PR.
	OutcomeFlagged = "flagged"
	// OutcomeBudget: the Codex budget is at or past [usage] codex_soft; no
	// later case should start either.
	OutcomeBudget = "budget"
	// OutcomeSkipped: the case is not replayed, since an earlier case of the
	// run hit a usage limit, needed a login or reached the Codex budget, or
	// the run was interrupted; `magnum eval run` records it so.
	OutcomeSkipped = "skipped"
)
    Case outcomes of a replay besides the round's (pipeline.Outcome*), which
    evalrun.RunCase records (OutcomeSkipped: `magnum eval run`) and the daemon's
    gate of a skill proposal reads.

const FlaggedFile = "flagged.json"
    FlaggedFile holds the flagged cases (Flagged by case name) under the runs'
    root.

const RunIDFormat = "20060102-150405"
    RunIDFormat is a run id's time part: sortable, to the second.


FUNCTIONS

func AgentTag(id string) string
    AgentTag tags the agents of run id (agents.Deps.Tag): "eval-" and the
    first 6 hex digits of the id's SHA-256, the same for all the run's cases.
    The tag joins the agents' names' hash, so they are named apart from the
    PR's own agents and from every other run's: StartAgent adopts an agent that
    carries a role's name, and a run once adopted the agents the run before it
    left behind. It also leads their titles and pane labels.

func FullReplayFor(runs []Run, caseName, head string, like *Run) (Run, CaseRun, bool)
    FullReplayFor finds the replay a judge-only replay of case caseName at head
    takes its reviewers' reports from: the newest run whose case of that name
    reviewed head with every role (not JudgeOnly), ended a scored dry run and,
    unless like is nil, whose reviewers read what the judge-only replay's would,
    like's (ReviewedOtherwise: the same reviewer inputs and notes setting).
    A nil like takes any such run, so a refusal can name the newest. runs are
    oldest first (ListRuns); ok is false when none did.

func HashNotes(file, dir string) (map[string]string, error)
    HashNotes is the SHA-256 (hex) of each notes file a replay gives the judge:
    the repository's notes file, keyed by its base name ("" when there is none),
    and every regular file under its harness directory dir, keyed by the
    directory's base name and the path below it ("web/qa.sh"). Two runs whose
    maps differ for a case gave its judge other notes (WriteText says so).

func LoadFlagged(root string) (map[string]Flagged, error)
    LoadFlagged reads the flagged cases under root by case name; a missing file
    is none.

func MarkFlagged(root string, f Flagged) error
    MarkFlagged adds f to the flagged cases under root (the first record of a
    case stands).

func NewRunDir(root string, now time.Time) (id, dir string, err error)
    NewRunDir creates the directory of a run started at now under root and
    returns the run's id and directory. The id is now to the second, with "-2",
    "-3"... when a run started in the same second holds it (os.Mkdir fails
    with ErrExist), so no two runs share a directory, a record or an agent tag
    (AgentTag).

func ReplayedAt(r Run, cr CaseRun) time.Time
    ReplayedAt is when run r replayed its case cr: the case's start, else the
    run's (zero when neither was recorded). A run can outlive many of its cases'
    replays (the skill gate replays a lost guard's base into the base run it
    made at its first baseline), so its own start dates only its first.

func SaveRun(dir string, r Run) error
    SaveRun writes dir/run.json atomically (a temporary file in dir, then a
    rename), mode 0600; dir is created with mode 0700.

func WriteCorpus(path string, c Corpus) error
    WriteCorpus writes c to path as TOML that LoadCorpus reads back as c,
    atomically (a temporary file, then a rename) with mode 0600, creating
    the directory (0700). A corpus LoadCorpus would refuse is not written,
    and a file that already holds the same text is left as it is.

func WriteMarkdown(w io.Writer, r Run)
    WriteMarkdown writes the report of r as markdown (report.md): a summary
    table, then per case each defect as found or missed with its severity,
    and the findings that matched no defect.

func WriteText(w io.Writer, r Run, prev *Run)
    WriteText writes the human report of r: a table with one row per case
    and a total, how many absent defects were hit (when the run has any),
    the Codex points the cases used, then, when prev is not nil, how the totals
    moved since it and which cases read other notes than in prev, then one line
    per missed defect, per absent defect hit and per case error.


TYPES

type Baseline struct {
	Run    string    // the stored run's ID
	Commit string    // magnum's commit that ran it
	Case   CaseRun   // the case as that run recorded it
	At     time.Time // when the run replayed the case (ReplayedAt)
}
    Baseline is a stored replay of a case that a run with the same inputs need
    not repeat.

func Baselines(runs []Run, inputs string, c Case) []Baseline
    Baselines lists, newest run first, the stored replays of c that a run with
    inputs (Run.Inputs: the judge skill, the roles' prompts, the role config,
    the stakes lines and the simplification caps) may reuse instead of replaying
    c: runs that recorded the same inputs from a clean checkout, whose case
    of c's name reviewed c's head with every role (not a judge-only replay,
    CaseRun.JudgeOnly) and has a score. Unknown inputs ("") reuse nothing.
    The inputs leave magnum's code out, so the caller decides whether the code
    of Commit reviews as its own does (eval-at.sh compares the Go files of the
    two commits).

func JudgeBaselines(runs []Run, inputs string, c Case, reports string) []Baseline
    JudgeBaselines lists, newest run first, the stored replays of c whose
    judge read inputs on the reviewer reports of run reports (the full replay a
    judge-only replay of c takes them from, FullReplayFor): that run's own case
    of c when it recorded inputs, and judge-only replays of c on its reports
    (CaseRun.ReportsRun) that recorded inputs; clean runs with a score only,
    as for Baselines. Comparing a judge-only candidate with one of these,
    never with another full replay, keeps the reviewers' variance between two
    full replays out of the comparison.

type Case struct {
	Name    string   `toml:"name"`           // unique, [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}
	PR      string   `toml:"pr"`             // owner/repo#N
	Head    string   `toml:"head"`           // the reviewed head, 40 lower-case hex
	Base    string   `toml:"base,omitempty"` // base branch name, optional
	Why     string   `toml:"why,omitempty"`  // why the case is in the corpus, optional
	Defects []Defect `toml:"defect"`

	// Owner, Repo and Number are parsed from PR.
	Owner  string `toml:"-"`
	Repo   string `toml:"-"`
	Number int    `toml:"-"`
}
    Case is one pull request pinned to the head that is reviewed, with the
    defects a review must find.

func (cs *Case) Validate() error
    Validate reports every rule cs breaks, as LoadCorpus does for a corpus that
    holds it, and fills Owner, Repo and Number from PR; nil when cs is valid.

type CaseRun struct {
	Case       string    `json:"case"`
	PR         string    `json:"pr"`
	Head       string    `json:"head"`
	Outcome    string    `json:"outcome"` // dry_run, error, needs_attention, usage_limit, skipped, ...
	Error      string    `json:"error,omitempty"`
	ResultFile string    `json:"result_file,omitempty"` // absolute path of the judge result
	ReportDir  string    `json:"report_dir,omitempty"`
	Started    time.Time `json:"started,omitzero"`
	Finished   time.Time `json:"finished,omitzero"`
	Score      *Score    `json:"score,omitempty"` // nil when there was no result to score
	// Notes is what notes the judge read (HashNotes): file -> SHA-256, "" for a notes file there
	// was none of; nil when the run withheld them (Run.NoNotes) or did not record them.
	Notes map[string]string `json:"notes,omitempty"`
	// CodexBefore and CodexAfter are the Codex budget used (percent, in Codex's whole points) as
	// the gauge read when the case started and when it ended; nil when it could not be read. The
	// gauge counts every Codex session of the account, live rounds included.
	CodexBefore *float64 `json:"codex_before,omitempty"`
	CodexAfter  *float64 `json:"codex_after,omitempty"`
	// JudgeOnly: the judge alone reviewed, on the reviewers' reports of the case in run ReportsRun,
	// the newest full replay of it at the same head (FullReplayFor; `magnum eval run --judge-only`).
	JudgeOnly  bool   `json:"judge_only,omitempty"`
	ReportsRun string `json:"reports_run,omitempty"`
}
    CaseRun is one case of a replay: what became of the review round and,
    when it left a result, the score.

func (c CaseRun) Points() (float64, bool)
    Points is how far the Codex gauge moved while the case ran; ok is false when
    either reading is missing or the window reset in between (the gauge fell).

type Corpus struct {
	Cases []Case `toml:"case"`
}
    Corpus is the set of pull requests with seeded defects a replay is scored
    against.

func LoadCorpora(user, learned string) (*Corpus, error)
    LoadCorpora reads the operator's corpus at user ("" = none) and the
    learned corpus the daemon writes at learned (paths.Layout.LearnCorpus;
    "" or a file that does not exist adds nothing) and returns their cases,
    the user's first. A case name in both files is an error that names it.
    Without a user corpus and without learned cases the error is the learned
    file's. One path given as both (a run given the learned corpus as --corpus,
    scored again) is read once.

func LoadCorpus(path string) (*Corpus, error)
    LoadCorpus reads and parses the corpus file at path.

func (c *Corpus) Select(names []string) ([]Case, error)
    Select returns the cases called names, in corpus order; no names selects
    every case. A name the corpus does not know is an error.

type Defect struct {
	ID    string `toml:"id"`    // unique within the case, same charset as a case name
	Title string `toml:"title"` // shown in reports
	// Severity is, for a defect to find, the weakest severity that still counts as right; for an
	// absent one, the weakest at which a matching finding is a hit (a weaker one is neither a hit
	// nor noise). P0..P3, optional.
	Severity string   `toml:"severity,omitempty"`
	Paths    []string `toml:"paths,omitempty"`  // globs on the slash path, "**" spans directories
	Lines    []int    `toml:"lines,omitempty"`  // inclusive head-side range [from, to]
	Match    []string `toml:"match,omitempty"`  // case-insensitive regexps on the finding body
	Body     bool     `toml:"body,omitempty"`   // a mention in the review body also counts; needs Match
	Expect   string   `toml:"expect,omitempty"` // ExpectFound ("" too) or ExpectAbsent

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Defect is one thing a review must report, or with Expect ExpectAbsent one
    it must not. A finding matches it when its path matches one of Paths (any
    path when empty), its range comes within three lines of Lines (any line when
    empty) and one of Match matches its body (anything when empty). Paths and
    Match must not both be empty.

type DefectResult struct {
	ID         string `json:"id"`
	Title      string `json:"title"`
	Want       string `json:"want,omitempty"` // the defect's severity
	Found      bool   `json:"found"`
	By         []int  `json:"by,omitempty"`       // indexes into Result.Findings that matched
	Severity   string `json:"severity,omitempty"` // the strongest among matching inline findings, "" if none
	SeverityOK bool   `json:"severity_ok"`        // found, and at Want or stronger (or no Want)
}
    DefectResult is the outcome for one defect of a case.

type Finding struct {
	Path           string `json:"path,omitempty"`
	Line           int    `json:"line,omitempty"`
	StartLine      int    `json:"start_line,omitempty"` // 0 = single line
	Body           string `json:"body"`
	Severity       string `json:"severity,omitempty"`       // P0..P3 or ""
	Simplification bool   `json:"simplification,omitempty"` // an optional suggestion, never a defect
	InBody         bool   `json:"in_body,omitempty"`        // the review body rather than an inline comment
}
    Finding is one thing the review reported: an inline comment, or the review
    body as a whole.

type Flagged struct {
	Case   string    `json:"case"`
	PR     string    `json:"pr"`
	Head   string    `json:"head"`
	Run    string    `json:"run"`
	Reason string    `json:"reason"`
	At     time.Time `json:"at"`
}
    Flagged is a case whose replay was refused: in which run, at which head,
    why and when.

func FlaggedCase(flagged map[string]Flagged, c Case) (Flagged, bool)
    FlaggedCase is the flagged record of case c: the one of its name, else one
    of its PR (owner/repo#N, letter case aside), so a refused PR stays out under
    another case name.

func (f Flagged) Refusal() string
    Refusal says why the case is not replayed.

type Replay struct {
	Run    string
	Inputs string
	At     time.Time
	Case   CaseRun
}
    Replay is a stored replay of a case (NewestReplay): the run that made it,
    the inputs that run recorded (Run.Inputs, "" before they were), when it
    replayed the case (ReplayedAt) and the case as the run recorded it.

func NewestReplay(runs []Run, c Case, skip string) (Replay, bool)
    NewestReplay is the newest stored replay of c at the head the corpus pins
    that has a score, a full or a judge-only one, from a clean checkout or not,
    leaving out the runs that recorded inputs skip ("" leaves none out;
    the skill gate leaves out its candidate's own): the one replayed last
    (ReplayedAt), in whatever run, two dated alike ordered by their runs (oldest
    first: ListRuns) and within a run by their order. ok is false when there is
    none.

type Result struct {
	Status   string
	Event    string
	Counts   map[string]int // the "findings" object: severity -> number
	Findings []Finding      // inline comments in order, then the review body when it is not empty
	Planned  bool           // planned_review was present
}
    Result is what a judge result file says about one round.

func ParseResult(data []byte) (Result, error)
    ParseResult reads the judge's result file. The inline comments of
    planned_review become findings in order, followed by one InBody finding
    holding the review body when it is not empty.

    The severity of a comment comes from the provenance entry that was posted
    (or has no verdict) on the same path and line, else from the first P0..P3
    token in the first 80 characters of its body.

type Run struct {
	ID       string            `json:"id"`               // sortable, e.g. 20261004-153000
	Label    string            `json:"label"`            // free text
	Commit   string            `json:"commit"`           // magnum's git HEAD (short) when the run started, "" unknown
	Dirty    bool              `json:"dirty"`            // magnum's checkout had uncommitted changes
	Models   map[string]string `json:"models,omitempty"` // role name -> model, "" = the kind's default
	Corpus   string            `json:"corpus"`           // corpus path
	Started  time.Time         `json:"started,omitzero"`
	Finished time.Time         `json:"finished,omitzero"`
	Cases    []CaseRun         `json:"cases"`
	// Inputs identifies what the review read besides the PR and the notes: a hash of the judge
	// skill, the roles' prompts, the role config, the stakes lines and the simplification caps
	// (max_simplifications; "" in runs before it was recorded). Baselines matches on it.
	Inputs string `json:"inputs,omitempty"`
	// ReviewerInputs is the part of Inputs the reviewer roles read: their prompts, role config and
	// the stakes lines, the judges' and the simplification caps left out ("" in runs before it was
	// recorded). A judge-only replay takes the reports of a full replay whose reviewers read what
	// its own would (FullReplayFor).
	ReviewerInputs string `json:"reviewer_inputs,omitempty"`
	NoNotes        bool   `json:"no_notes,omitempty"` // no role was given the notes (--no-notes)
	// Candidate is the directory whose prompts and judge skill the run replayed (--candidate,
	// evalrun.WithCandidate); "" = the configured ones.
	Candidate string `json:"candidate,omitempty"`
	// CorpusAlone is set when the run read Corpus alone (--corpus FILE), without the learned corpus
	// the daemon writes; `eval score` reads it alone again. Runs before it was recorded read both.
	CorpusAlone bool `json:"corpus_alone,omitempty"`
}
    Run is one replay of a corpus.

func ListRuns(root string) ([]Run, error)
    ListRuns loads every root/*/run.json, oldest ID first. A directory without a
    readable run.json is skipped; a missing root has no runs.

func LoadRun(dir string) (Run, error)
    LoadRun reads dir/run.json.

func Rescore(r Run, c *Corpus, read func(path string) ([]byte, error)) Run
    Rescore recomputes the score of every case of r from its saved result
    file against the current defects of the corpus, so a corrected match
    expression takes effect without running the agents again. read loads a file
    (os.ReadFile when nil). The run it returns is a copy; r is not changed.

    A case the corpus no longer has, or that has no result file, keeps its
    score. A case the corpus now pins to another head than the run reviewed
    keeps its score (the defects name the new head's lines), and so does a
    result that cannot be read or parsed; either sets Error to say so when the
    case has a score or no other error. A rescore that succeeds clears an Error
    an earlier one set.

func RunsBefore(runs []Run, t time.Time) []Run
    RunsBefore is runs as they stood at t: each run with only the cases it
    replayed before t (ReplayedAt; an undated replay counts as before), a run
    left with none dropped. A zero t keeps them all. runs is not changed.

func (r Run) ReviewedOtherwise(like Run) string
    ReviewedOtherwise says how r's reviewers read other inputs than like's
    would ("" = they read the same): other reviewer inputs (ReviewerInputs;
    a run that recorded none, from before they were recorded, counts as other),
    or the notes given where like withholds them or withheld where like gives
    them (NoNotes: the reviewers' prompts point at the notes too). The notes'
    content is not compared: it moves with every curation, and a judge-only
    replay measures a judge change on the same reports, not on the notes the
    reviewers read then.

func (r Run) Totals() Totals
    Totals adds up the scores of the run. Cases without a score count in Cases
    only.

type Score struct {
	Case            string         `json:"case"`
	Status          string         `json:"status,omitempty"`
	Event           string         `json:"event,omitempty"`
	Defects         []DefectResult `json:"defects"`
	Found           int            `json:"found"`
	Total           int            `json:"total"`
	Noise           int            `json:"noise"`               // inline findings that matched no defect, simplifications aside
	Simplifications int            `json:"simplifications"`     // optional simplification suggestions, neither defect nor noise
	Unmatched       []Finding      `json:"unmatched,omitempty"` // the noise findings
	// Absent counts the case's absent defects (Defect.Expect ExpectAbsent), which Defects, Found and
	// Total leave out; AbsentHits are the ones a finding reported, each a false positive (the
	// findings that hit them are not noise).
	Absent     int            `json:"absent,omitempty"`
	AbsentHits []DefectResult `json:"absent_hits,omitempty"`
}
    Score is the outcome for one case.

func ScoreCase(c Case, r Result) Score
    ScoreCase tells, for every defect of c, whether the findings of r report it.
    An inline finding matches a defect when its path matches one of the
    defect's paths (any when none), its line range comes within three lines
    of the defect's lines (when set) and its body matches one of the defect's
    regexps (when set). A review body matches only a defect with body = true,
    by its regexps alone, and only with its finding list and nearby block
    (bodyFindings). Simplification suggestions match nothing and are not noise.
    One finding may match several defects. An absent defect (expect =
    "absent") is matched the same way, but a finding that matches it is a hit
    (Score.AbsentHits) when the defect has no severity or the finding is at it
    or stronger (or has none to compare); a weaker one is the finding ranked as
    it should be. Neither is noise, and absent defects count in neither Found
    nor Total.

func (s Score) SeverityOK() int
    SeverityOK counts the found defects that were reported at the wanted
    severity or stronger.

type Totals struct {
	Cases           int // all cases of the run
	Scored          int // cases that have a score
	Found           int
	Total           int
	Noise           int
	Simplifications int
	SeverityOK      int
	Recall          float64 // Found/Total, 0 when Total is 0
	Absent          int     // absent defects of the scored cases (Score.Absent)
	AbsentHits      int     // the ones a finding reported (Score.AbsentHits): false positives
}
    Totals sums the scored cases of a run.

```

## evalrun

```text
package evalrun // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/evalrun"

Package evalrun replays one case of an eval corpus (internal/eval) as a blind
dry-run round and scores it: what `magnum eval run` does for each case,
in a package the daemon can call too. Each case runs in its own scratch layout
(registry, reports, a copy of the notes) under the run's directory and in a
detached worktree of the repository's clone, with agents tagged for the run,
so the live registry, the PR's own agents, another run's agents and the PR's
reports are never touched. A candidate directory (WithCandidate) replays another
checkout's prompts and skill.

CONSTANTS

const (
	// OutcomeFlagged: the case is not replayed: an earlier replay of it or
	// of its PR was refused (eval.FlaggedCase), or the live registry holds
	// a Codex flag for its PR (Refused).
	OutcomeFlagged = eval.OutcomeFlagged
	// OutcomeBudget: the Codex budget is at or past [usage] codex_soft
	// (Options.Force runs anyway); no later case should start either.
	OutcomeBudget = eval.OutcomeBudget
	// OutcomeError: the case could not run (the round's error outcome).
	OutcomeError = pipeline.OutcomeError
)
    Case outcomes of RunCase besides the round's (pipeline.Outcome*).

const CandidateSkill = config.CandidateSkill
    CandidateSkill is where a candidate directory holds the judge skill,
    as magnum's checkout does.

const ReleaseTimeout = 2 * time.Minute
    ReleaseTimeout bounds closing a case's agents after its round.


VARIABLES

var ErrNoFullReplay = errors.New("no full replay to take the reviewers' reports from")
    ErrNoFullReplay is a judge-only replay's error when it finds no scored full
    replay of its case at the same head whose reviewers read what its own would
    to take the reviewers' reports from, or the one it finds left none.


FUNCTIONS

func Inputs(cfg *config.Config) string
    Inputs is a hash (12 hex) of what a replay's review reads besides the PR
    and the notes (eval.Run.Inputs): every role's config with the model it
    resolves to and its kind's config, the prompt files the roles name as
    they resolve now (the checkout's prompts_dir, else the embedded ones),
    with the judge prompts' partials file (config.SharedPrompt) their blocks
    come from, each judge's skill file, the stakes lines of the [[watch]] and
    [[repo]] blocks (what the judge and the reviewers size a harm against),
    and the simplification caps the judge posts by: the pipeline table's
    max_simplifications in effect and each [[repo]] block's that is set
    (config.Config.MaxSimplificationsFor), and with [jira] on the site and
    the account the judge reads the PR's ticket from (not the token file).
    The texts count, not where they are: a judge's skill path is left out of its
    role config, so a candidate directory with the same texts as the checkout
    has its inputs (a landed candidate's replays are the next baseline).
    magnum's own code is not part of it. "" without a config.

func Refused(ctx context.Context, d Deps, ec eval.Case) string
    Refused says why case ec is not replayed ("" = it may be): an earlier
    replay of it or of its PR, under any case name, was refused (the runs root's
    eval.FlaggedFile, which cannot be read refuses too), or the live registry
    holds a Codex flag for its PR (liveFlag).

func ReviewerInputs(cfg *config.Config) string
    ReviewerInputs is the part of Inputs the reviewer roles read
    (eval.Run.ReviewerInputs): the same hash over the roles that are not judges,
    with the stakes lines the reviewers read too and without the simplification
    caps and [jira], which only the judges read, so a change to a judge's
    prompts, skill, caps or ticket leaves it alone and a judge-only replay can
    take the reports of a full replay whose reviewers read what its own would
    (eval.FullReplayFor). "" without a config.

func RunCase(ctx context.Context, d Deps, ec eval.Case, o Options) (out eval.CaseRun)
    RunCase replays case ec and scores it. Every failure becomes the case's
    outcome (OutcomeError, OutcomeBudget, OutcomeFlagged or the round's);
    a refused replay is flagged (eval.MarkFlagged) so that it never runs again.
    It starts nothing for options without an absolute RunDir or an AgentTag
    (checked first), for a case Refused names, of a repository no watch covers,
    or whose candidate is no candidate. One replay of a case runs at a time,
    whoever starts it (`magnum eval run`, eval-at.sh through it, the daemon's
    gate): it holds the case's lock (lockCase) from its first check to the end
    of its cleanup, a second replay of the case waiting for it, and Started is
    when it took the lock.

func RunsRoot(l paths.Layout) string
    RunsRoot is where a layout's eval runs live: <state>/eval/<run id>/,
    with the flagged cases (eval.FlaggedFile) and the cases' worktrees (wt/)
    (paths.Layout.Eval).

func WithCandidate(cfg *config.Config, dir string) (*config.Config, error)
    WithCandidate is the config a replay of candidate dir reviews with
    (config.Config.WithCandidate, which the skill editor's checks share):
    a copy of cfg (config.Config.WithoutSnapshot: read from disk, whatever the
    daemon loaded at startup) whose prompts_dir is <dir>/prompts and whose every
    judge reads <dir>/skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md, both absolute. dir is a
    checkout or a worktree of magnum with a change to the prompts or the skill;
    a prompt it lacks resolves to the embedded default, as in any checkout.
    An error when dir has no prompts directory or no skill file; cfg is never
    changed.


TYPES

type Deps struct {
	// Layout is the install's: its logs, locks and gh config directories,
	// the live notes a case copies and the runs root (RunsRoot). A case's
	// scratch layout is a copy of it with Scratch set.
	Layout paths.Layout
	// Config is the config the case reviews with (WithCandidate's for
	// Options.Candidate is applied by RunCase).
	Config *config.Config
	// Store is the live registry, read for the PR's Codex flag only; nil =
	// the registry file at Layout.DB(), opened read-only for each check
	// (never created).
	Store *store.Store
	// Logger is the case app's logger (nil = warnings and errors as text to
	// Stderr).
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Stderr receives the case app's human-readable logs (app.Options).
	Stderr io.Writer
	// Now is the case's clock (nil = time.Now).
	Now func() time.Time
	// Runner replaces the case app's subprocess runner (app.Options; nil =
	// the real one).
	Runner execx.Runner
	// Progress reports a step of the case ("fetching ...", "reviewing in
	// ..."), Warn a problem that does not end it (a worktree left behind,
	// agents that stay open); nil = none.
	Progress func(format string, args ...any)
	Warn     func(format string, args ...any)
}
    Deps is what a replay works with.

type Options struct {
	// Candidate replays a candidate directory's prompts and skill
	// (WithCandidate); "" = Config's.
	Candidate string
	// JudgeOnly runs the judge alone on the reviewers' reports of the
	// case's newest full replay at the same head whose reviewers read what
	// this replay's would (eval.FullReplayFor: ReviewerInputs of the config
	// the case reviews with, and NoNotes), copied into the case's report
	// directory (engine.EvalCase.JudgeOnly); a case without one, or whose
	// full replay left no reviewer report, fails with ErrNoFullReplay before
	// it reads GitHub or checks anything out.
	JudgeOnly bool
	// NoNotes withholds the repository notes from every role; Keep leaves
	// the case's worktree in place; Force runs past [usage] codex_soft.
	NoNotes, Keep, Force bool
	// AgentTag tags the case's agents (agents.Deps.Tag), the run's own;
	// required, so the agents are never named as the PR's own.
	AgentTag string
	// RunDir is the run's directory (RunsRoot/<run id>), an absolute path:
	// the case's scratch tree is RunDir/cases/<case>, and a refused replay
	// is flagged under the run's id, its base name.
	RunDir string
	// Worktrees is the directory the case's worktree goes in,
	// Worktrees/<case> (caseWorktree); "" = RunsRoot/wt, `magnum eval
	// run`'s. The daemon's gate gives its own
	// (paths.Layout.LearnEvalWorktrees), so the two never replace each
	// other's worktree of a case.
	Worktrees string
}
    Options are a case's settings, the run's.

```

## execx

```text
package execx // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/execx"

Package execx is the single choke point for every subprocess magnum runs (git,
gh, mysql, mise exec, launchctl, osascript, codex/claude probes).

Every call carries a timeout, runs in its own process group so a cancelled
context terminates the whole tree (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL), gets an explicit
env overlay and a working directory, captures at most MaxOutput per stream,
and logs a redacted transcript. Tests use Fake; --dry-run wraps the real runner
in DryRun so mutating commands are printed instead of run.

CONSTANTS

const DefaultTimeout = 2 * time.Minute
    DefaultTimeout applies when Cmd.Timeout is zero.

const MaxOutput = 8 << 20
    MaxOutput caps each captured stream (stdout and stderr separately). Output
    past it is drained and discarded so the child never blocks on a full pipe;
    the kept prefix is followed by TruncationMarker and Result.Truncated is set.

const TruncationMarker = "\n[execx: output truncated at 8 MiB]\n"
    TruncationMarker is appended to a stream cut at MaxOutput.


FUNCTIONS

func EventLevel(level string) slog.Level
    EventLevel is the slog level of an audit event's level ("debug", "info",
    "warn", "error"; anything else is info), for the line that mirrors the event
    in the log.

func FailLevel(ctx context.Context, err error) slog.Level
    FailLevel is the level of a line that reports err, a failure the caller
    tolerates: slog.LevelWarn, or slog.LevelInfo when err is the daemon stopping
    (IsStop), which cuts short every call in flight and is no fault.

func IsStop(ctx context.Context, err error) bool
    IsStop reports whether a failure is the daemon stopping rather than a fault:
    ctx ended (a shutdown cancels it, an abort cancels a round's) or err says
    the work was canceled.

func LogAt(l Logger, level slog.Level, format string, args ...any)
    LogAt sends one line to l: at level through Logf when l is a LevelLogger,
    else through Printf (a plain Logger has no levels). A nil l drops it.

func LogEvent(l Logger, level, subject, kind, line string)
    LogEvent mirrors an audit event to l as line: at the event's level
    (EventLevel), with its subject and kind as attributes when l is an
    AttrLogger, else as LogAt sends it. The caller redacts line.
```
